questions.q: What is an ecosystem defined as?
a: A community of living organisms interacting with each other and their non-living physical environment
Only the animals living in a specific desert
The total number of plants in a forest
The non-living rocks and soil of a planet

questions.q: Which term describes the living components (such as plants, animals, and fungi) within an ecosystem?
a: Abiotic factors
Biotic factors
Atmospheric factors
Geological factors

questions.q: What are abiotic factors in an ecosystem?
a: Living predators and prey
Parasitic bacteria and fungi
Non-living physical and chemical components such as temperature, light intensity, and moisture
Decomposers breaking down dead matter

questions.q: What is the primary source of energy for almost all life on Earth?
a: Geothermal heat
Nuclear power
Deep ocean vents
The Sun

questions.q: What term describes organisms that make their own food using light energy through photosynthesis (e.g., plants and algae)?
a: Producers (autotrophs)
Primary consumers
Secondary consumers
Decomposers

questions.q: What is a consumer in a food chain?
a: An organism that produces its own glucose via sunlight
An organism that gets its energy by feeding on other organisms
A non-living mineral source
A fungus that absorbs nutrients externally

questions.q: Which organism type feeds directly on producers (plants) and is classified as a primary consumer?
a: Carnivore
Apex predator
Herbivore
Decomposer

questions.q: What term describes an animal that eats other animals (carnivores or herbivores)?
a: Producer
Herbivore
Autotroph
Carnivore

questions.q: What does a food chain show?
a: The transfer of energy and nutrients from one organism to the next, starting with a producer
The migration paths of birds across continents
The chemical composition of soil minerals
The classification of rocks in geology

questions.q: What is a food web?
a: A single straight line of predator-prey relationships
An interconnected network of many food chains within an ecosystem
A diagram showing weather patterns
A map of global human populations

questions.q: What role do decomposers (such as bacteria and fungi) play in an ecosystem?
a: They produce oxygen through photosynthesis
They hunt primary consumers for sport
They break down dead organic matter and recycle essential nutrients back into the soil
They consume rocks to create sand

questions.q: What is represented by the arrows in a food chain or food web diagram?
a: The direction the animals run
Who eats whom for fun
The path of water movement
The direction of energy and biomass transfer between organisms

questions.q: What is a trophic level?
a: The position an organism occupies in a food chain or food web
The geographical altitude of a mountain habitat
The temperature of ocean water
The speed at which an animal moves

questions.q: What percentage of energy is typically passed on from one trophic level to the next in a food chain?
a: 100 percent
Roughly 10 percent
50 percent
99 percent

questions.q: What happens to the majority of energy (about 90 percent) as it moves up from one trophic level to the next?
a: It is stored forever in bones
It is converted into heavy metals
It is lost to the environment through respiration, movement, and heat loss
It disappears from the universe entirely

questions.q: Why are food chains rarely longer than four or five trophic levels?
a: Animals get bored of eating
There is too much oxygen at the top
Top predators refuse to hunt
Energy is severely depleted at higher levels, insufficient to support further top carnivores

questions.q: What is a pyramid of numbers?
a: A diagram showing the relative number of individual organisms at each trophic level in an ecosystem
A chart showing human birth rates
A calculation of total dry mass in a forest
A geological rock formation

questions.q: Why can a pyramid of numbers sometimes be inverted (upside down)?
a: Because numbers always decrease upwards
Because a single large producer (like a large oak tree) can support thousands of smaller primary consumers (like insects)
Because energy flows backwards
Because consumers are heavier than producers

questions.q: What is a pyramid of biomass?
a: A chart showing air pressure at different heights
A diagram of animal population counts
A diagram showing the total dry mass of living biological material at each trophic level
A map of desert plant distribution

questions.q: What term describes the place where an organism naturally lives and obtains its resources?
a: Biosphere
Population
Community
Habitat

questions.q: What is a population?
a: All the organisms of a particular species living in the same area at the same time
Every living thing on planet Earth
Only the carnivores in a jungle
The non-living soil and water in a lake

questions.q: What is a community in ecological terms?
a: A group of human houses
All the different populations of living organisms interacting within a particular habitat
A single organism surviving alone
The climate zone of a continent

questions.q: Which abiotic factor measures the degree of hotness or coldness of an environment, directly affecting enzyme activity in organisms?
a: Wind speed
Soil pH
Temperature
Altitude

questions.q: How does light intensity affect plant distribution in a forest ecosystem?
a: Plants do not need light at all
Plants grow best in total darkness
Light has no effect on plant growth
Higher light intensity in open areas increases the rate of photosynthesis for sun-loving plants

questions.q: What is an ecological niche?
a: The role, function, and position of an organism within its ecosystem, including its interactions with biotic and abiotic factors
The physical hole an animal digs in the ground
The geographical border of a country
The weight of an apex predator

questions.q: Which gas in the atmosphere is essential for aerobic respiration by animals and plants?
a: Carbon dioxide
Oxygen
Nitrogen
Methane

questions.q: Which gas is absorbed by plants from the atmosphere during photosynthesis?
a: Oxygen
Hydrogen
Carbon dioxide
Helium

questions.q: What term describes the recycling of carbon atoms between living organisms and the atmosphere through processes like photosynthesis, respiration, and combustion?
a: The water cycle
The nitrogen cycle
The rock cycle
The carbon cycle

questions.q: How do animals return carbon dioxide to the atmosphere?
a: Through cellular respiration
By performing photosynthesis
By drinking river water
By absorbing sunlight through skin

questions.q: What role do fossil fuels play in the carbon cycle when burned?
a: They absorb excess carbon dioxide
They release large quantities of stored carbon dioxide into the atmosphere rapidly
They purify polluted air
They turn into solid rock

questions.q: Why is nitrogen gas (N2) from the air not directly usable by most plants and animals?
a: It is too heavy to breathe
It is toxic to living cells
It is unreactive due to strong triple covalent bonds between nitrogen atoms
It is liquid at room temperature

questions.q: Which type of soil bacteria converts nitrogen gas from the air into nitrates that plants can absorb?
a: Denitrifying bacteria
Lactic acid bacteria
E. coli bacteria
Nitrogen-fixing bacteria

questions.q: What is competition in ecology?
a: The struggle between organisms for limited environmental resources such as food, water, light, or mates
A cooperative partnership between two species
The process of photosynthesis in leaves
The migration of birds south for winter

questions.q: What is interspecific competition?
a: Competition between members of the exact same species
Competition between individuals of different species for the same limited resources
Competition between plants and rocks
Competition for sunlight in deep caves

questions.q: What is intraspecific competition?
a: Competition between lions and hyenas
Competition between trees and grass
Competition between members of the same species for resources like food, shelter, or mates
Competition between fish and birds

questions.q: What is mutualism?
a: A relationship where one organism kills another for food
A relationship where a parasite harms its host
A relationship where one species benefits while the other is killed
A close biological interaction where both participating species benefit from the relationship

questions.q: Which of the following is a classic example of a mutualistic relationship?
a: Cleaner fish eating parasites from the teeth of large sharks
A tapeworm living inside a human intestine
A lion hunting a zebra
Grass being eaten by a rabbit

questions.q: What is parasitism?
a: A relationship where both species help each other
A relationship where one organism (the parasite) benefits at the expense of another (the host)
A relationship where neither organism is affected
A process where plants make food

questions.q: What is biodiversity?
a: The total weight of rocks in a region
The speed of river currents
The variety and abundance of different species living within a particular ecosystem or on Earth
The temperature range of a desert

questions.q: Why is high biodiversity important for the stability of ecosystems?
a: It makes ecosystems boring to study
It guarantees that no animals will ever die
It causes rapid climate change
It helps ecosystems withstand environmental changes and disease outbreaks because alternative species can maintain ecological functions
